Diego / team — quick shortlist and sizing (high-level, conservative):

1) redwood-3-small (baseline)
- Recommended context: 2048 tokens
- Latency profile: good at <250ms p95 for single-turn with batching disabled at 12 qps on a single A100 equivalent pipe
- Cost/estimate: assume compression via prefix caching ~10% token reduction
- Tokens/month (pilot conservative): 150 users active -> assume 10k daily interactions total -> average tokens per interaction 360 -> monthly = 10,000 * 360 * 30 = 108,000,000 tokens -> apply 1.15 safety factor => ~124M tokens/month
- Ops note: excellent stability; no quantization needed for quality-sensitive clinical summaries

2) redwood-3-medium (higher quality / longer context)
- Recommended context: 8192 tokens (useful for longer multi-turn summaries)
- Latency profile: expect ~350-450ms p95 at 12 qps; recommend p95 provisioning (dedicated pool) for pilot
- Tokens/month: if 20% of sessions use long context (2k extra tokens/session), conservative monthly = base 124M + 0.2 * 10,000 * 2,000 * 30 = 124M + 120M = ~244M tokens/month
- Ops note: recommend 1-2 dedicated GPUs (or Redwood Dedicated slot) for predictable latency; consider KV caching for repeated context

3) open-7b-4q (quantized open candidate for cost optimization)
- Recommended context: 2048 tokens
- Latency profile: comparable p95 when colocated; better cost per token but verify fidelity on clinical summaries
- Tokens/month: use same baseline as redwood-3-small => ~124M tokens/month
- Ops note: run a short eval on clinical subset (5-10 prompts) before pilot; if hallucination risk acceptable, run as fallback for low-cost paths

Extra: if ClearHealth expects many multi-turn threads (more than 3 turns/session) scale context to 12k and model to redwood-3-large for summary quality — we'd need to re-run sizing.

Attachments: model_shortlist_notes.pdf (includes quick benchmark notes and example prompts).

Priyom — if you have quant/throughput tweaks (batching, micro-batching, autoscale window) please add.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Ella — quick summary and next steps based on our internal sizing. See attached: mutual_action_plan_ClearHealth.docx, model_shortlist_notes.pdf, and we kept your token_profile on file.

Summary (conservative):
- Recommended shortlist: redwood-3-small (baseline), redwood-3-medium (for longer-context summaries), open-7b-4q (low-cost fallback)
- Pilot conservative tokens/month: 124M (baseline usage with redwood-3-small) up to ~244M if ~20% sessions use extended 2k context and redwood-3-medium is used for those flows.
- Latency expectations: redwood-3-small can hit <250ms p95 with proper routing and no heavy batching; redwood-3-medium may be ~350-450ms p95 — recommend a dedicated slot for the medium variant during the pilot.
- Ops recommendations: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated patient prompts, set autoscale to cover 20 qps headroom, enable per-route tracing for early regressions.

Next steps:
1) Kickoff meeting — propose Thu Aug 27 at 10:00 AM PST (let me know if this works).
2) Quick clinical-file eval: we need 20 representative prompts (anonymized) for a short fidelity check on open-7b-4q if you want to include it as fallback.
3) DOCS/Compliance: Grace will follow up with private deployment guidelines and KMS checklist.

Let me know when you want the MAP executed — we can lock a Dedicated slot for the pilot once the MAP is signed.
